text.p: Steel fabricator and recycler Metalcorp Ltd said on Wednesday trading results for the four months to end-October were about 20 percent down on a year ago.
Metalcorp said directors would review the interim dividend when half-year results were available, but expected it would be affected by the difficult trading conditions to date.
However, the company said it expected a much improved performance for the second half of the current financial year.
Metalcorp said its steel merchandising division had traded strongly over the four months, and the shortfall could be attributed to its metal recycling division.
This was due to lower ferrous scrap prices, lower non-ferrous scrap intake, supply problems with major customers and lower exports than expected.

However, it said many of the problems in recent months were not expected to recur, and the company was pursuing clear initiatives to promote growth. "As a result, Metalcorp anticipates a much improved performance for the second half of the current financial year," it said.
Metalcorp shares were 11 cents lower at A$1.84 at 12.40 p.m. (0140 GMT).
